sections.title: Executive Summary
sections.content: India's artificial intelligence industry is forecast to reach more than $7 billion by the end of 2026 [E1]. While 62 percent of Indian enterprises report using artificial intelligence at scale for product development [E2], the sector faces challenges, including a potential shortage of more than 1.4 million artificial intelligence professionals by 2026 [E3]. Organizations must navigate an evolving regulatory landscape that includes the Digital Personal Data Protection Act and proposed artificial intelligence governance guidelines (verify the current status) [E4][E5].

sections.title: Market Insights
sections.content: The Indian artificial intelligence industry is expected to grow to more than $7 billion by the end of 2026 [E1]. Supporting this growth, operational data center capacity in India expanded from approximately 375 megawatts in 2020 to roughly 1.5 gigawatts in 2025 [E6]. Enterprise artificial intelligence infrastructure spending reached approximately $18 billion in 2025 [E7]. Demand is driven by business leaders, with 76% believing that Generative Artificial Intelligence will have a significant business impact [E8]. Despite this, over 95% of organizations allocate less than 20% of their information technology budgets to artificial intelligence [E9]. Workforce constraints remain a primary concern, as 45% of Indian organizations identify artificial intelligence, digital, and data skills as their single largest constraint [E10].

sections.title: Competitor Analysis
sections.content: The accepted evidence does not identify enough verified companies providing products or services in the Artificial Intelligence market to support a company-level competitor comparison. Funding and investor activity may provide market context, but do not establish that an organisation is a competitor.

sections.title: Opportunities and Risks
sections.content:
Opportunities:
• Nearly 60% of organizations are now co-innovating with startups to advance their AI capabilities [E11].
• Seventy-six percent of business leaders believe that Generative AI (a type of AI that can create new content) will have a significant impact on their business [E8].
• With 0.97 billion internet connections in India as of June 2024, there is a vast digital foundation for AI adoption [E12].
Risks:
• India could face a shortage of more than 1.4 million AI professionals by 2026, with 82% of employers reporting difficulty filling roles [E3][E13].
• Only 25% of Indian organizations believe their current workforce is adequately prepared to use AI effectively [E14].
• New regulations, such as the proposed Artificial Intelligence (Ethics and Accountability) Bill, 2025, introduce potential penalties of up to 50 million rupees for non-compliance (verify the current status) [E15].

sections.title: Recommendations
sections.content:
• Invest in internal training programs to address the 82.9% Generative Artificial Intelligence skills gap, as only 25% of Indian organizations believe their workforce is currently prepared to use artificial intelligence effectively [E14][E16].
• Prioritize rapid deployment strategies for new artificial intelligence projects, given that 91% of business leaders identify speed as the most critical factor in their decision to buy or build solutions [E17].
• Establish a robust compliance framework to align with the Digital Personal Data Protection Act and the India Artificial Intelligence Governance Guidelines to mitigate risks associated with the proposed penalties for artificial intelligence misuse (verify the current status) [E15][E4][E5].

sections.title: Glossary
sections.content:
Simple explanations of important terms used in this report. These definitions are explanatory notes, not research evidence.
- Artificial Intelligence: This refers to computer systems designed to perform tasks that typically require human intelligence.
- Generative Artificial Intelligence: This is a type of artificial intelligence technology capable of creating new content such as text, images, or code.
- Digital Personal Data Protection Act: This is a legislative framework in India designed to regulate the processing and protection of personal digital data.
- Data Center: This is a specialized facility used to house computer systems and associated components for data storage and processing.
- Co-innovating: This describes the process where two or more organizations collaborate to develop new products or services.
- Compliance Framework: This is a structured set of guidelines and processes that an organization follows to ensure it meets legal and regulatory requirements.
